subject: Civil Engineering
title: Soil Nailing: Stitching the Ground
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Soil Nailing: Stitching the Ground.

hook.text: Instead of building a wall, what if you reinforced the soil itself to stand on its own?

buildup.text: Soil nails are steel bars drilled into a slope and grouted in place.

discovery.text: The nails bond with the soil and resist sliding — turning the slope into a gravity wall.

twist.text: Shotcrete facing covers the surface — a thin shell over reinforced ground.

climax.text: Soil nailing stabilized highway cuts across the mountains of Switzerland.

punchline.text: Nail the soil in place and the slope holds itself up.

quiz.question: How do soil nails stabilize a slope?
options: They drain water out of the slope to reduce weight
Steel bars grouted into the soil resist sliding forces like internal reinforcement
They freeze the soil in place using liquid nitrogen
